simple.meaning: זָקֻן (zâqun) is a Hebrew word meaning “old age.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: זָקֻן (H2208) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Genesis 21:2, with occurrences in Genesis.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to זָקֻן (H2208) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in זָקֻן (H2208) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: זָקֻן (zâqun) / H2208 is traced through Genesis 21:2, Genesis 21:7, Genesis 37:3, Genesis 44:20 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Sarah conceived, and bore Abraham a son in his old age, at the set time of which God had spoken to him.

majorEvents.label: Birth or introduction
majorEvents.evidenceText: She said, “Who would have said to Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? For I have borne him a son in his old age.”

timeline.evidenceText: Sarah conceived, and bore Abraham a son in his old age, at the set time of which God had spoken to him.
She said, “Who would have said to Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? For I have borne him a son in his old age.”
Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age, and he made him a tunic of many colors.
We said to my lord, ‘We have a father, an old man, and a child of his old age, a little one; and his brother is dead, and he alone is left of his mother; and his father loves him.’
